scope: Deterministic native-engine physics at 120 Hz; fictional damage calibration, no claim of vehicle-engineering fidelity.
checks: New damage arrays sanitize, deep-copy and default to healthy for older saves.
Localized moderate collisions bend alignment and reduce the struck spring/damper and brake, before a wheel detaches.
Bent alignment produces physical steering pull while coasting; even a damaged car cannot rotate from steering at rest.
Worn brakes lengthen the measured stop and asymmetric brake damage creates a real yaw reaction.
A damaged corner has less travel, weaker damping and a lower settled ride height; curb response remains bounded.
Respawn, car switching and serialized saves preserve each damaged part; repair resets alignment, suspension and brakes without free fuel or NOS.
A lobby damage-off rule prevents new impact, shift and overrev wear while keeping fuel use and already damaged condition.
